## Design

### 2026-10-20 – Following the guide i made my own schematic and took the tips to make it look cleaner overall, also due to the low amount of pins i decided to sacrifice the LEDs pin for an extra button and yes i know

**3h**

Following the guide i made my own schematic and took the tips to make it look cleaner overall, also due to the low amount of pins i decided to sacrifice the LEDs pin for an extra button and yes i know i can make a matrix but it wouldn't make sense in this case since i'm making a 3*2 button matrix wich would barerly save any pins specifically only 1 and also simply because i want it to be nice and compact

### 2026-10-21 – After finishing the schematic i went to the pcb part where i had to make some capacitive touch things with exposed copper basically wich was a problem because it took so much to find a good looking, o

**3.6h**

After finishing the schematic i went to the pcb part where i had to make some capacitive touch things with exposed copper basically wich was a problem because it took so much to find a good looking, original yet small design because i want my piano to be as small and portable as possible but also look good and function well so it took a while because i scrapped a lot of designs that didn't meet my requirements, in the end i chose these dimensions (in the pictures) wich save space, look good and yeah that's pretty much it, i tried to be as  precise as possible, avoided making them too close to each other and they turned out good, after that i placed all the other footprints and from here i will start routing and placing components on the board. Forgot to mention i also added a courtyard so no components overlap on them
